level1.text: A green laser pointer emits light of wavelength $532\,\text{nm}$. What is the momentum of one photon? Give the answer in units of $10^{-27}\,\text{kg}\cdot\text{m/s}$.

The molybdenum anode of an X-ray tube strongly emits X-rays of wavelength $0.0711\,\text{nm}$. What is the momentum of a photon of this radiation? Give the answer in units of $10^{-24}\,\text{kg}\cdot\text{m/s}$.
The momentum of a photon is $3.60 \cdot 10^{-27}\,\text{kg}\cdot\text{m/s}$. What is the wavelength of the photon? Give the answer in nanometres.
The momentum of a photon is $2.00 \cdot 10^{-27}\,\text{kg}\cdot\text{m/s}$. What is the energy of the photon? Give the answer in units of $10^{-19}\,\text{J}$.

A laser of power $1.0\,\text{mW}$ emits photons, each of energy $3.14 \cdot 10^{-19}\,\text{J}$. How many photons does the laser emit per second? Give the answer in units of $10^{15}\,\tfrac{1}{\text{s}}$.

level2.text: An X-ray photon of wavelength $0.0711\,\text{nm}$ scatters from an almost free electron in graphite. The wavelength of the scattered photon is $0.0735\,\text{nm}$. How much kinetic energy does the electron receive? Give the answer in electronvolts.
The decay of caesium-137 produces a gamma photon of energy $662\,\text{keV}$. What is the momentum of the photon? Give the answer in units of $10^{-22}\,\text{kg}\cdot\text{m/s}$.

The wavelength of infrared light travelling in an optical fibre is $1550\,\text{nm}$. A photon hits a mirror perpendicularly and is reflected straight back. How much momentum does the mirror receive from one photon? Give the answer in units of $10^{-28}\,\text{kg}\cdot\text{m/s}$.

A sensitive light detector counts $2.40 \cdot 10^{4}$ photons per second. The wavelength of the light is $550\,\text{nm}$. What is the power of the light arriving at the detector? Give the answer in units of $10^{-15}\,\text{W}$.

level3.text:
In laser cooling, laser light of wavelength $589\,\text{nm}$ is directed against a sodium atom. The atom absorbs one photon at a time, and each photon reduces the momentum of the atom by the momentum of the photon.

The mass of the sodium atom is $3.82 \cdot 10^{-26}\,\text{kg}$, and its initial speed is $3.00 \cdot 10^{2}\,\text{m/s}$.

How many photons must the atom absorb to stop? Assume that all the photons come straight against it, and ignore the effect of the photons re-emitted by the atom, because they leave in random directions. Give the answer in units of $10^{4}$.

An X-ray photon of wavelength $0.0500\,\text{nm}$ scatters from an almost free electron. The electron receives the kinetic energy $1.00\,\text{keV}$. What is the wavelength of the scattered photon? Give the answer in nanometres to four decimal places.

A hydrogen atom at rest moves from the energy level $n = 3$ to the level $n = 2$ and emits a photon. The energy levels of hydrogen are $E_n = -\tfrac{13.6\,\text{eV}}{n^2}$. The atom receives a momentum equal in magnitude to that of the photon and in the opposite direction, that is, a recoil. What is the speed of the atom after the photon has left? The mass of a hydrogen atom is $1.67 \cdot 10^{-27}\,\text{kg}$. Give the answer in metres per second.
